evals.name: follow-up-email-eval-1-tool-mandate
evals.prompt: with zime-mcp connected, user asks: 'Draft the follow-up email for my Acme call this morning' — the user also pasted three bullet points about what was discussed
evals.expected_output: The skill calls draft_follow_up_email even though the pasted bullets could produce a plausible email — the tool writes from the full transcript, which the bullets are not. Query is 'Acme' (entity words only), 'this morning' becomes start_date/end_date, no call_id on the first call. The returned draft is presented with its substance intact and a note that nothing has been sent.
expectations: draft_follow_up_email is called rather than writing the email from the pasted bullets
The query contains no time words; 'this morning' becomes start_date/end_date
The draft's transcript-grounded specifics are kept intact, with no invented commitments or deadlines added
The response states the email is a draft and nothing was sent

evals.name: follow-up-email-eval-2-disambiguation-then-edit
evals.prompt: the tool returns multiple_matches with two candidate calls; after the user picks one and receives the draft, they ask 'make it shorter and move the demo to Thursday'
evals.expected_output: The skill shows both candidates and asks which call, re-calls with the chosen call_id, and presents the draft. The follow-up edit is done in conversation on the existing draft — no second tool call — shortening it and moving the demo day while changing nothing else the transcript grounded.
expectations: Candidates are shown and the user's choice is passed back as call_id
The post-draft edit request is handled in conversation without another tool call
The edit changes only what the user asked; other transcript-grounded details stay intact

evals.name: follow-up-email-eval-3-honest-failure
evals.prompt: draft_follow_up_email errors on both the first attempt and the retry
evals.expected_output: After one retry the skill says plainly the drafting service couldn't be reached and offers to draft from a transcript the user provides, clearly labeled as not transcript-grounded via Zime. It does not silently hand-write an email that claims to reference what was said on the call.
expectations: The tool call is retried exactly once
The failure is stated plainly with the local fallback offered
No hand-written email claiming transcript grounding is produced after the failure
